## Findings
- claim-1: The 2024 paper defines integral \(\Lambda\), \(I_{r,n-r}\), \(\overline\Lambda=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and states Theorem 1.2: for every bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(J_v\) is minimally generated by \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110]
- claim-2: In the Grassmannian model, \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) corresponds to \(i^j\), and \(r\)-Grassmannian Bruhat containment is Young-diagram containment; the integral quotient has Schur basis indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 779-834] [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 847-862]
- claim-3: The requested target is established: both original Theorem-4.8 families are minimal generators of the actual integral ideal \(J_v\), including \(i=n-r\) or \(j=r\).
## Strategy
**Proof certificate.** Put \(q=n-r\), \(R_{r,q}:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and \(\bar s_\lambda\) for the Schur image. The quotient has integral basis
\[
R_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
\]
[doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 828-834].

Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\). The original hypotheses
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n
\]
are those for \(v\) [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-74]. They imply
\[
i,j\ge1,\quad r-j=t-1\ge0,\quad
q-i=n-r-s+t-1\ge0,
\]
the last because the strict integral inequality gives \(t\ge r+s-n+1\). Hence
\[
1\le i\le q,\qquad1\le j\le r.
\]

Write \(\iota:R_{r,q}\hookrightarrow H^*(\mathrm{Fl}_n,\mathbb Z)\) for the Grassmannian inclusion and
\[
K_v:=J_v\cap\iota(R_{r,q}).
\]
The full flag ring has Schubert \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{\sigma_u\}\), \(J_v\) is the coordinate span of \(\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\), and \(\iota(R_{r,q})\) is the coordinate span of the \(r\)-Grassmannian classes. Intersecting two coordinate submodules of a free module intersects their indexing subsets. Since \(r\)-Grassmannian permutations correspond to \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), and \(u\ge v\) is equivalent to \(\lambda\supseteq i^j\), one obtains
\[
K_v=
\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}
\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
=:J_{r,q;i,j}.
\]
Here the correspondence and Bruhat-containment statement are source-backed at
[doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 847-862].
Moreover, Littlewood–Richardson containment gives
\(c_{\lambda,\nu}^{\rho}\ne0\Rightarrow\lambda\subseteq\rho\); therefore this interval span is an ideal, since every surviving quotient term still contains \(i^j\).

For the integral involution, set
\[
H(z)=\sum_{m\ge0}h_mz^m,\qquad E(z)=\sum_{m\ge0}e_mz^m,
\qquad H(z)E(-z)=1,
\]
with \(h_0=e_0=1\) and negative indices zero. Coefficient recursion shows inductively that every \(e_m\in\mathbb Z[h_1,\dots,h_m]\). Thus \(h_m\mapsto e_m\) defines an integral endomorphism \(\omega\) of \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\dots]\). Applying it coefficientwise gives
\[
E(z)\,\omega(E(-z))=1.
\]
But \(H(-z)E(z)=1\); uniqueness of the inverse of \(E(z)\in\Lambda[[z]]\), whose constant term is \(1\), yields
\[
\omega(E(-z))=H(-z),\qquad \omega(e_m)=h_m.
\]
Hence \(\omega^2=\mathrm{id}\).

For \(\ell=\ell(\lambda)\), Jacobi–Trudi is
\[
s_\lambda=\det(h_{\lambda_a-a+b})_{1\le a,b\le\ell}.
\]
Dual Jacobi–Trudi is
\[
s_\mu=\det(e_{\mu'_a-a+b})_{1\le a,b\le\mu_1}.
\]
Taking \(\mu=\lambda'\), both determinants have size \(\ell(\lambda)\), so
\[
\omega(s_\lambda)
=\det(e_{\lambda_a-a+b})_{1\le a,b\le\ell(\lambda)}
=s_{\lambda'}.
\]
Thus \(\omega\) is an integral ring involution. Rectangle transposition gives
\[
\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r},\qquad
\bar\omega_{r,q}:R_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{q,r},
\quad\bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}.
\]
Also
\[
i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda',
\]
including empty-rectangle cases. Consequently, basiswise,
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}.
\]

Define the transformed bigrassmannian parameters
\[
r^\dagger=q,\qquad t^\dagger=q-i+1,\qquad
s^\dagger=q-i+j.
\]
Then
\[
1\le t^\dagger\le r^\dagger,\qquad
t^\dagger\le s^\dagger,\qquad
r^\dagger=q\le n,\qquad
s^\dagger=q-i+j\le q+r=n,
\]
and
\[
t^\dagger-(r^\dagger+s^\dagger-n)=r-j+1>0.
\]
Thus every transformed bigrassmannian inequality holds. Its associated parameters are
\[
i^\dagger=s^\dagger-t^\dagger+1=j,\quad
j^\dagger=r^\dagger-t^\dagger+1=i,
\]
and
\[
a^\dagger=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b^\dagger=b.
\]

Theorem 1.2 states that
\[
\mathcal F_{\downarrow}:=
\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}
\]
is minimal [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110]. Applied to \(v^\dagger\), it makes the corresponding lower family in \(J_{q,r;j,i}\) minimal. Transposition maps that family bijectively to
\[
\mathcal F_{\rightarrow}:=
\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
\]
because \((j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\). The ring isomorphism therefore transfers minimality to \(\mathcal F_{\rightarrow}\) in the actual interval ideal \(J_{r,q;i,j}=K_v\).

Finally, the Grassmannian contraction and the full-flag \(J_v\) have equivalent generation and minimality for Grassmannian elements [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 84-88]. Hence both families minimally generate the original full-flag basic ideal \(J_v\).

If \(a=0\), then \(q-i=0\) or \(r-j=0\), i.e. \(i=q\) or \(j=r\). Both displayed families reduce to \(\{\bar s_{i^j}\}\). This class is nonzero because \(i^j\subseteq q^r\), so it belongs to the quotient Schur basis. The preceding theorem and isomorphism arguments therefore include these boundary cases.

## Gaps
None relative to the supplied DOI passages and the integral Jacobi–Trudi argument.

## Next
The requested target is established: both original Theorem-4.8 interval families are minimal generators of the actual integral ideal \(J_v\), including \(i=q\) or \(j=r\).
